title: Define compatibility assertions and version-fallback contract for new open-model ingestion
creator: Ava Kim
description: Clarify product requirements for how new open models (community/contributed weights) are ingested into the Redwood model catalog with explicit compatibility assertions and an unambiguous version-fallback contract. Goal: reduce runtime regressions, make automated routing safe, and give runtime/ops predictable fallback behavior without ad-hoc pinning decisions. This ticket defines the contract that intake owners must collect, the annotation surface in the catalog, runtime expectations, and acceptance criteria for admission. It also captures trade-offs between faster admission and the risk of runtime incompatibilities.
acceptance_criteria: A concise compatibility schema that intake form enforces at ingest time and is stored as top-level catalog fields: declared_api_surface, max_sequence, kv_cache_compatibility, quantization_profile, kernel-recommendation, license_provenance_hash, expected_memory_gb, fallback_priority_list

Runtime mapping rules documented: when a request matches a model variant, runtime uses fallback_priority_list to select alternatives; if a chosen fallback has different 'declared_api_surface' the runtime must perform a compatibility shim or reject with a mapped error code (CATALOG_INCOMPAT)

Two-tier ingestion flow described: fast-triage (metadata-only + smoke-run) vs full-admit (profiling, kernel selection, sample-prompt evals). Admission UI shows which tier was used and lists any skipped checks
Onboarding checklist items enforced: example prompt set (10 prompts), deterministic latency/memory smoke test on reference hardware, license provenance entry, and a signed artifact hash for weights

Clear pin semantics documented: strong-pin (no auto-fallback allowed), soft-pin (runtime may fallback to compatible variant if quality regression is within configured delta), unpinned (runtime free to route to cheaper/compatible variants), and automatic rollback sentinel semantics
Backward-compatible runtime behavior specified for legacy catalog entries (migration plan and compatibility-flag defaults)

2026-03-01: Trade-off agreed: require only a 10-prompt sample set for initial admission to keep time-to-admit low; full evals can be gated behind canary release
2026-03-04: Security requested signed weight artifact and license_provenance_hash; accepted as gating requirement for public community models

notes_for_engineering: Implement schema validation at ingest-time with clear error codes: MISSING_FIELD, INCOMPAT_TYPE, SIGNATURE_MISSING
Add a lightweight smoke-run job that runs on the same hardware type used for initial profiling and records latency, peak memory, and kv-cache-hits for the sample prompts
Expose fallback selection logs to the console with route_reason and compatibility_mismatch fields for postmortems
Provide a migration script that assigns default compatibility flags to legacy entries and surfaces a migration dashboard for catalog owners
